certainty_reasoning: Cook states the marriage as fact in passing while describing the Ives household; no date, place or maiden name is given on the page read.
date_label: Married before the household years; date not stated in the source read
summary: James Goddard married Sylvie and brought her into George Ives's household, where they raised two daughters known as 'the 2 Kit girls'. Cook records that Ives's relationships with the men of the house began possibly sexually before settling into something he framed as paternal - and that the households's men, Goddard among them, married without leaving it.

sources.quote: 'Kit' (James Goddard) had been a servant at the Ives' family seat in Hampshire and then moved with George to London. When he married he bought his wife Sylvie into the household too; 'the 2 Kit girls' were their daughters.
sources.context: Cook's roll-call of the Ives household. 'bought' is printed thus in the source, evidently for 'brought'; transcribed as printed.
sources.supports: The marriage, Sylvie's entry into the household, and the two daughters
sources.provenance: PDF p. 107 (printed folio 96 confirmed on the rendered page).

sources.quote: Kit and his wife Sylvie kept house for Ives in a relatively familiar – though rapidly diminishing – tradition of live-in domestic service. … James and Sylvie Goddard remained with Ives until their deaths; their daughters until the early 1940s.
sources.context: Cook on the Adelaide Road household. The same page adds that the daughters left to open a shop with money Ives had settled on their father, and that Therese was still visiting in 1944, when Ives called her 'the youngest of my adopted family - and she is 47!' (which would put her birth about 1897).
sources.supports: Cook reportedly records that Sylvie kept house for Ives, that she and James remained until their deaths, and that the daughters stayed until the early 1940s - one, Therese, still visiting in 1944. Known so far only from the PDF text layer; verify at the rendered page before quoting.
sources.provenance: PDF page 111, printed folio 100 confirmed in the running head on the rendered page ('100 Queer Domesticities').
